This lot of Rulindo Murambi was grown by more than 170 family owned farms in Rwanda's Gatsibo district. Smallholder farmers bring their cherries to the centralized Murambi washing station where they are processed with safer, more modernized machinery than individual farmers are able to access. Murambi begins the processing with the quality control method of hand sorting and floating the cherries in water. They are then depulped and fermented. The fermentation process is halted by a 18-24 hour freshwater soak, after which the parchment is washed for a second time. Washing station workers perform a final round of quality control by meticulously hand sorting the parchment on pre-drying tables while it is gently dried to the touch. After removing any parchment with defects from the lot, they transfer it to fully exposed drying tables for 14-21 days.
We love this coffee's bright opening plum notes, which meld into smooth dark chocolate and the rich sweetness of brown sugar. Brew it as a pourover for more prominent fruit notes or try it as espresso to bring out its complex chocolate flavor!

Story
+
-
Marysabel Caballero and Moisés Herrera are the magnanimous couple behind Finca El Puente. Marysabel, a fourth-generation coffee farmer, met Moisés, an accountant, when he was sent to manage the Honduran operations of a Guatemalan coffee company. They fell in love, married, and established Finca El Puente on land in Chinacla. Over the years, their enterprise has grown, but they remain steadfast in their dedication to caring for their land, their product, and their community. The efforts have paid off: coffee from Finca El Puente has won many awards and is regularly featured in premier cafes across the globe.
One of the qualities that makes Moisés and Marysabel such exceptional partners is their constant drive to improve. They're always refining every aspect of their coffee production. Recently, they made small adjustments to their processing that reduced water use while subtly changing the flavor profile of their signature coffee. With mechanical demucilagers, they left a bit more mucilage on the parchment than in previous years. This type of processing is most similar to honey processing. That small change has brought a brighter, fruitier character to the cup.
Though Finca El Puente is known for growing and testing unique coffee varieties, this coffee is 100% Catuai, the most popular variety on their farm. This year’s offering sings with notes of apricot, blackberry, and chocolate.

Sourced from indigenous coffee-producing communities in the Tenejapa region of Chiapas, this lot reflects the distinct identity of Mexican coffee. The region’s high elevations, volcanic soils, and rich cultural heritage shape both the land and its coffee.
The state of Chiapas is Mexico’s southernmost coffee-growing region, bordered by Guatemala to the east and the Pacific Ocean to the south. Its landscape is marked by the Sierra Madre de Chiapas, a mountain range that rises from coastal plains into high-altitude forests, creating a remarkable diversity of microclimates and ecosystems. Protected areas such as El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve, home to one of the last remaining cloud forests in Central America, highlight the region’s rich biodiversity.
Coffee cultivation in Chiapas is concentrated in these highlands, where elevations between 1,200 and 1,800 meters above sea level, coupled with fertile volcanic soils, provide ideal conditions for Arabica varieties. Shade-grown under native trees, coffee here benefits from abundant rainfall and moderate year-round temperatures, factors that encourage slow cherry development and a complex cup profile.
Chiapas is also defined by its cultural heritage. Indigenous communities, including Tzeltal and Tzotzil Maya groups, play a central role in coffee production, often farming small plots of land passed down through generations. Their traditions, combined with sustainable practices and community-led cooperatives, make Chiapas one of Mexico’s most distinctive and celebrated coffee origins.

This year marks 30 years since Marysabel Caballero and Moises Herrera began their journey together in coffee. To celebrate, we are bringing back La Tortuga, a name first used in 2004 for coffee from Marysabel’s father, Don Fabio, as a nod to the classic story of the tortoise and the hare. What began as a reflection on Honduras’s steady rise in specialty coffee now speaks to the Caballero family’s approach to building their coffee legacy: patient, deliberate, and always moving forward. That spirit of progress comes through in this latest release of Batian, a prized Kenyan variety with genetics that include SL28, SL34, and Sudan Rume. Through selective picking, careful sorting, and washed processing, Marysabel and Moises bring remarkable clarity to the variety. The result is one of our favorite La Tortuga selections of the year. It's a compelling expression of Kenyan genetics adapted to Honduran terroir.

A HIGH ELEVATION PACAS SEPARATION FROM A YOUNG PRODUCER IN SANTA BÁRBARA
While visiting Juan Angel in 2022, we learned that he bequeathed his highest elevation parcel, La Montaña, to his eldest son Irvin. Madcap has purchased coffee from Juan’s family since 2014, and as time has marched on, his sons have become more involved with coffee production. For the fifth year, we are honored to release this special micro-lot coffee under Irvin Izaguirre’s name.
La Montaña sits at 1,850 MASL, high above its neighboring farms in Santa Bárbara primarily producing the Pacas variety. Blazing sun paired with constant cool breeze create an ideal terroir for slow cherry maturation and complex coffee. The parcel is not accessible by car, so cherries are transported by mule down the mountainside along narrow footpaths bag by bag. Besides the elevated quality of La Montaña lots, harvesting and processing requires much more labor and care, so the family receives premiums for the separation of Irvin's coffee.

About
Santuário Sul sits in the hills of Carmo de Minas, built as a deliberate step away from traditional Brazilian coffee. The project was founded by Luiz Paulo Dias Pereira, alongside collaborators including Camilo Merizalde, with the intention to experiment , both in the field and at the mill.
Rather than focusing on volume, Luiz Paulo approaches the farm as a living collection of varieties. More than 30 cultivars are planted across the property, each managed separately and monitored closely through harvest. This level of control allows the team to refine how each variety responds to altitude, soil, and process, with Luiz personally cupping early samples to guide decisions.
Pacamara is a clear example of this intent. A variety not traditionally associated with Brazil, it’s grown here with careful attention to maturation , and fermentation. This Pacamara present s high sweetness and a coating mouthfeel , shaped through an extended fermentation protocol .
The result is a different expression of Brazil , less familiar and more exploratory, and firmly tied to a producer willing to test the limits of what can be done.
How to Drink: Just like you wouldn't add soda to your best whiskey, this amazing coffee is meant to be drank black with no sugar or cream.

Details
The Story
Direct Trade
See all
See all
Producer: Juan Peña
Farm: Hacienda La Papaya
Region: Loja Province
Altitude: 2,100 masl
Varietal: Typica, Pacas, Caturra, Catuaí, and San Salvador
Process: Anaerobic Natural
Roast: Light-Medium
Notes: Black Cherry, Cocoa Powder, Kumquat
B7 refers to the seventh "bloque" (lot) planted at Hacienda La Papaya. It is located in one of the highest areas of the farm, at 2,100 meters above sea level, and gets sunlight through most of the day. Whereas the rest of the lots are single varietals, B7 is a mix of Typica, Pacas, Caturra, Catuaí, and San Salvador.
Our green coffee buyer visited Hacienda La Papaya in August and had this to say: "The B7 lot is quite a cult fave now. Juan was going to tear it up and replant it with a single variety, like the other 'Bloques' (he's up to 16 now). It's the only Bloque that is a natural 'blend.' Add 120 hours of anaerobic natural processing to it and it becomes really unique. Only a handful of roaster partners worldwide get this coffee."
After being harvested, selected, and cleaned, the cherries go to polyethylene tanks to ferment after oxygen is forced out. The tanks are shaded so that temperatures during fermentation are not allowed to exceed 24° C (75° F). After fermenting, the cherries are transferred to drying rooms for approximately 30 days.
Fifth-generation farmer Juan Peña began planting coffee in 2009 and now has 16 hectares of coffee in production at Hacienda La Papaya in Loja, Ecuador. The coffee is fully irrigated and fertilized according to an ingenious system of Juan's design, with soil sensors that analyze the ideal fertilization mixture at any given time. There is also an extensive nursery on site which serves both to regenerate existing lots and nurture new varietals.
Along with Philip Smith, Juan Peña founded CafExporto in 2019 at first to serve as the exporting arm of La Papaya. It has now expanded to offering technical and educational support, processing expertise, and export services for producer partners in Loja, Zamora, and other regions throughout the country. We visited Hacienda La Papaya and CafExporto most recently in August 2026.
Coffee FAQs
How soon will my coffee ship?
All of our coffees are roasted to order. Orders placed before 4PM Central roast + ship the next business day. Orders placed after 4PM Central on Thursday will roast + ship on Monday.
How much does shipping cost?
Single 10oz bags of coffee are eligible for $3 USPS Ground Advantage shipping or faster $5 Flat Rate shipping.
Coffee orders under $50 ship via $5 Flat Rate.
Coffee orders over $50 ship free in the US!
More Details
Can you grind my coffee for me?
We recommend ordering Whole Bean and grinding just before you brew for best results. But if you don't have a coffee grinder yet, we're happy to grind it for you. We offer two grind sizes for our Limited Offerings:
• Auto: a medium grind suitable for automatic drip coffee makers.
• Coarse: a coarse grind suitable for French press, cold brew, and percolators.
Check out our Brew Guides for tips on popular methods.
Can I subscribe for recurring delivery of this coffee?
Due to limited inventory, this coffee is not eligible for recurring orders. Browse our Subscribe + Save collection here .

Jorge Rojas has dedicated his life to coffee since he was 12 years old, and was always focused on producing high-quality coffee while keeping ecological farming practices at the forefront. Rojas received his organic BIO certificate through ASEPOP Planadas,a 275-member coop in which provides its members with processing and QC resources, educational training, and various opportunities to travel to trade shows around the country.
We’re excited to carry more coffees from Jorge Rojas this year. We recently carried his washed Gesha from another one of his farms in Planadas, Finca La Roca, and last year we had his pink bourbon from this same farm, El Jardín. We tried several different Chiroso microlots of his earlier harvested earlier this year, which are meticulously separated by lot for fine-tuned drying processes. Unlike Lot 6 currently on the menu, this lot has a more mellow, caramelized profile. This lot was fermented for 12 hours in cherry, then depulped and left to ferment for 16 more hours in mucilage. The precision in fermentation and drying processes is evident in the resulting cup profile. We get clean, crisp notes like green apple and star fruit, with a lingering sweet caramel finish.

All our roasted coffees are run through an AI-powered optical sorter. This extra step ensures that you receive only the most nutrient-dense, flavorful coffees from each lot. The machine is also capable of removing any foreign objects (corn, metals, rope, to name a few) from the rest of the coffees.
The higher the percentage, the more coffee is being removed in order to achieve a truly pristine product. We liken this to how sake-makers "polish" during production in order to reach a higher-quality product.
Nothing goes to waste: the rejected coffees are re-roasted and sold to local markets.

Chiroso
Originally from the region of Urrao, Antioquia, Chiroso is thought to be a mutation from Caturra. Known to some as the "Pink Bourbon" of Antioquia, Chiroso's stand at the world stage for their clarity and intensity of expression.

PROCESSING
Hand-picked at peak ripeness. Floated. Held in-cherry for 12 hours in shade. De-pulped and cleaned. Dry-fermented in plastic barrels for 12 hours. Wet-fermented for an additional 12 hours. Meticulously hand-washed to remove mucilage only. Dried in shade until moisture content reaches ~10%.
ABOUT DANCHE
Neguesse Debela began operating his first site in Worka Chelbessa in 2017, later expanding in 2019 with the purchase of a second washing station a few kilometers away in the small sub-region of Danche. Both sites produce exceptional washed and natural coffees and are now developing experimental lots as part of an ongoing effort to further refine and elevate quality.
ABOUT ETHIOPIAN LANDRACE
Ethiopia is widely acknowledged as where coffee originated, and its production continues to represent a significant part of the country’s economy. DNA testing has confirmed over 60 distinct varieties growing in Ethiopia, making it home to the most coffee biodiversity of any region in the world. Given the tradition of coffee production in Ethiopia and the political interworkings of the Ethiopian coffee trade, it is virtually impossible to get single variety coffee lots from Ethiopia. This is changing, albeit very slowly. Most Ethiopian coffees are blends of the many Ethiopian varieties, and referred to simply as 'Ethiopian Landrace'.

As a subscriber, you get: 15% off all your orders, including one-time purchases First dibs when sold-out coffees are back in stock Early access to limited-release coffees Freebies and samples throughout your subscription Are you really roasting to order? Yes! We roast your coffee after you order to guarantee you receive it at peak freshness. On rare occasions, we may have small batches of pre-roasted coffee available—this is always clearly indicated on the product page under the roasting schedule section. Either way, you're getting exceptionally fresh coffee. How is your coffee sourced? The production of exceptional coffees is a collaborative, meticulous and multi-faceted effort. All coffees are sourced in freshly harvested lots through direct relationships with producers and cooperatives committed to quality and sustainable business practices. We travel to origin throughout the year, exploring new coffee sources, checking in with cherished producers, and offering premiums for quality. The long-standing partnerships we nurture are built upon trust—trust that our producers will convey to us what they need to thrive and trust that we will do everything we can to support them. Sightglass coffee tastes best up to six weeks after the roast date printed on the back of the sealed bag. Once opened, we recommend you use the coffee within two weeks for optimal freshness. We understand that each cup of coffee is unique and warrants the utmost attention to detail. That’s why we roast only in small batches. The Story
The Karumandi Coffee Factory sits just south of Mount Kenya amid emerald green fields of tea and countless small coffee farms. The nutrient-rich red volcanic soil, cool climate of the high elevation, and the fresh water of the Thiba River provide idyllic conditions for coffee cultivation. Coffee thrives in this region of Kenya and the staff of Karumandi are stewards to some of its best coffee.
Members of the Baragwi Farmer’s Cooperative Society, Karumandi purchases coffee from a network of approximately 3,000 smallholder producers. Agronomist Nicasius Ndambiri manages Karumandi and has been in this role for seventeen years. In addition to lending technical support for Karumandi’s many producers, Nicasius is also responsible for the highly technical work of overseeing the stages of processing. The gravity driven processing equipment can move approximately 7,000 kilos per hour at peak season.
Cherries are delivered and meticulously sorted at the mill, then undergo de-pulping and the wet fermentation process. Fermentation is carefully monitored and there are no static times––the process takes as long as it needs to––ranging from 17-30 hours. Once the process is complete, the coffee is laid to dry on a raised bed. The staff are currently renovating all 121 drying beds. Many of them are primarily made from the stocks of the nearby eucalyptus trees. These more durable metallic beds require less maintenance and provide a level surface for more even drying of the coffee. Once the coffee is dried, it’s transported to the New Kenya Planters Cooperative Union for final dry milling and lot building. Nicasius and Baragwi teams observe milling and cupping for transparency as the lots are graded and built.
The coffee from Karumandi is a celebration of everything Stumptown loves about Kenyan coffee!

Migration is created for cold brew, but fantastic as drip and espresso as well!
Our final version of Migration is here and might just be the best yet! We created a 50/50 blend with two of our lovely lots from Ethiopia. The first, a natural called Sasaba, is full of darker fruit, chocolate and berry notes. Our washed lot, Wuri is floral, citrusy and toffee sweet. Put them together in an even ratio and the aromatics shine with florals and mixed berries. Jasmine carries over into the cup and is joined by red grape and mango. Wrap all of this up in a fully body and juicy acidity and Migration is going out with a bang!
As always, Migration is great for cold brew and this version is banging! But definitely brew it up as espresso or drip. If you love coffee full of fruit character, you can't go wrong with Migration 9.2!
Transparency
1 Spot purchase
“Spot” is coffee in an importer’s inventory they have not sold. When we need to fill gaps in our contractual and relationship purchases, we buy spot. Of course, we are always open to spot becoming relationship purchases, and sometimes they do.
2 Contract purchase
Most of our purchases are contractual, meaning we have made a commitment to purchase the coffee before it arrives in the US. In general contracts are meant to build security for the producer and importer, and to help us make sure we have the coffee we need to share with you.
3 Repeat purchase
We are proud of the fact that many of the coffees we purchase are repeat purchases, and have been for years. Most producers, especially from Central and South America, can count on us purchasing their coffee year after year.
4 Visits
We’ve met, and have an ongoing relationship with the producer. At a minimum, they have visited us at Sweet Bloom, or we have visited them on the farm. As the relationship deepens, we build our understanding of:
1) challenges faced from one year to the next
2) sustainability practices on the farm
3) how the farmer is caring for their staff
4) ways in which we can support projects the farmers have implemented on the farm and in the community

Behind the Cup
Chispa combines two distinct Mexican coffees: washed La Perla from producers in Veracruz and Puebla, and anaerobic natural Río Verde from Guerrero. Río Verde undergoes a 36-hour anaerobic fermentation before drying. Together, the two processing approaches create a blend defined by fruit intensity, layered sweetness, and clean structure.
Each coffee is roasted to order. Orders ship within 2 business days.
Farmlevel Story
Created by Verve Coffee Roasters and Civil Coffee, Chispa brings together coffees from distinct growing communities across Mexico. La Perla works with producers in Veracruz and Puebla while supporting regional coffee production through its nursery and research programs, as well as the distribution of seedlings and organic compost. In Guerrero’s Sierra Madre, Río Verde comes from a remote community where coffee remains central to local livelihoods and environmental preservation.
Named for the Spanish word for “spark,” Chispa celebrates the connections behind the coffee, from the producers and communities who grow it to the longstanding friendship between Verve and Civil. The blend brings these relationships and distinct expressions of Mexican coffee into one shared offering.
